description: Per-service board for garret, the fleet's Nix binary cache on legion-node4 (docs/adr/0013). One scrape job, job="garret", with two targets distinguished by the `component` label: pusher (:9091) and puller (:9092). Metric names verified against garret rev 724ca56 (garret-server/src/{metrics,storage}.rs, garret-pusher/src/{main,gc}.rs, garret-puller/src/main.rs). Datasource is the fixed provisioned uid "victoriametrics"; the Logs row uses "victorialogs".

panels.title: Units up
panels.description: Scrape health of the two metrics listeners on legion-node4 (:9091 Pusher, :9092 Puller). 0 means the unit is down or unreachable.

panels.title: Bucket usage vs quota
panels.description: garret_gc_usage_bytes / garret_gc_quota_bytes, refreshed on every GC timer tick (the counter check is cheap; eviction is what is gated). Eviction starts at the high watermark (0.95) and runs down to the low one (0.85), so a steady reading in that band is the design point, not a problem.

panels.title: Stored bytes
panels.description: Bucket usage in bytes, as of the last GC timer tick (garret_gc_usage_bytes).

panels.title: Since last eviction pass
panels.description: Age of garret_gc_last_success_timestamp. Reads `never` under normal operation and that is correct: the GC timer only sets this gauge when a pass actually evicts, which it does only once usage crosses the high watermark (garret-pusher/src/gc.rs `tick` returns early below it). Treat it as "when did the quota last bite", not as a GC liveness check -- for liveness watch the usage gauge, which every tick refreshes.

panels.title: narinfo hit ratio (5m)
panels.description: Share of narinfo lookups the index could answer (garret_narinfo_requests_total outcome=hit). Misses are normal -- every substituter asks about paths no cache has -- so read this as a trend, not a target.

panels.title: narinfo lookups / s
panels.description: garret_narinfo_requests_total by outcome. This is what every `nix build` on the fleet hits first.

panels.title: NAR redirects / s
panels.description: garret_nar_redirects_total -- each one is a 302 to a presigned S3 URL, so the NAR bytes themselves never pass through this host or the edge.

panels.title: Presign latency
panels.description: garret_presign_duration_seconds. Sits directly on the substituter's critical path: every NAR fetch waits on it before the client can start downloading.

panels.title: Browse API and auth failures / s
panels.description: garret_browse_requests_total by endpoint (the Pocket ID-gated list/detail/tree/referrers routes) alongside garret_browse_auth_failures_total. Sustained failures usually mean an expired token or a Pocket ID client change, not an attack.

panels.title: Last-accessed bump failures / s
panels.description: garret_bump_failures_total. The LRU bump is fire-and-forget off the request path, so failures do not break substitution -- they starve GC of the access times it evicts by, which quietly makes eviction wrong.

panels.title: Upload outcomes / s
panels.description: Accepted, failed, shed (429 past maxConcurrentUploads) and skipped uploads. Skips are the good case: the negotiation step already had the path.

panels.title: Concurrency vs limits
panels.description: In-flight uploads against maxConcurrentUploads, and in-flight bytes ceiling. Riding the upload limit is what produces the shed rate on the left; the byte limit is the real memory bound on a 1.9 GiB node.

panels.title: Upload size
panels.description: garret_upload_bytes percentiles -- how big the NARs arriving here actually are, which is what partSize (32 MiB) and the 100 MB Cloudflare body limit have to fit.

panels.title: Upload duration
panels.description: garret_upload_duration_seconds percentiles: whole streaming PUT, including the S3 write.

panels.title: Negotiation
panels.description: Mean paths offered per negotiation call and the mean share of them the cache was missing. These two are summaries, not histograms (no bucket rule matches their names in garret-server/src/metrics.rs), so the panel averages _sum/_count rather than asking for a quantile.

panels.title: S3 operations / s
panels.description: Single PutObject calls, multipart parts, deletes and the multipart lifecycle. put failures rising while puts hold steady is the shape of an S3-side problem (credentials, throttling, MEGA S4 outage) rather than a garret one.

panels.title: S3 bytes uploaded / s
panels.description: garret_s3_bytes_uploaded_total -- counts both single PutObject bodies and multipart parts, i.e. everything billed as egress into the bucket.

panels.title: Part upload latency
panels.description: garret_s3_part_duration_seconds percentiles: one multipart part (32 MiB at the configured partSize) round-tripping to MEGA S4.

panels.title: Bucket usage vs quota
panels.description: garret_gc_usage_bytes against garret_gc_quota_bytes (250 GiB) over time. Usage steps rather than slopes: it is a SQLite total recomputed on each GC tick, not a continuously updated counter.

panels.title: GC work / s
panels.description: Objects and orphans removed per pass, plus stale multiparts aborted. candidates exhausted means GC ran out of evictable objects before reaching the low watermark -- the quota is then effectively unenforceable and the bill stops being bounded.

panels.title: Requests / s by status class
panels.description: garret_http_requests_total. Status is recorded as a class (2xx/4xx/...) rather than a code, deliberately, to keep series count bounded.

panels.title: Request latency p99 by route
panels.description: garret_http_request_duration_seconds. Routes are matched path templates, never concrete store paths.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: garret_http_requests_in_flight per unit.

panels.title: garret logs (pusher + puller)
panels.description: Journald logs for both units from VictoriaLogs (datasource uid 'victorialogs'), newest first. Filtered on the verbatim journald unit field _SYSTEMD_UNIT via in(...), same as the other per-service boards. 'Raw Logs' query type (/select/logsql/query).

title: garret (Nix binary cache)
